llm.summary: The skill appears to implement a read-only Stripe analytics tool and mostly matches its description, but there are inconsistent metadata/packaging signals (missing required-env in registry metadata vs package.json and SKILL.md) and some packaging omissions that warrant caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: The code and SKILL.md implement a read-only Stripe analytics dashboard and require a STRIPE_READ_KEY — that is coherent with the stated purpose. However, the registry metadata at the top of the report lists no required env vars or primary credential while package.json and SKILL.md both declare STRIPE_READ_KEY and node is required. This mismatch is a packaging/metadata inconsistency and should be resolved.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the implementation limit actions to reading Stripe endpoints (subscriptions, customers, invoices, plans, payment_intents). The instructions and code reference only Stripe API calls and do not instruct reading unrelated local files or extra environment variables. Error handling and pagination are described.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only) which is low-risk, but a code file (skill/skill.js) and package.json are included. package.json lists node as required binary; no external downloads or extraction are performed. The absence of an install spec combined with packaged code is an inconsistency worth verifying (how the host will execute this JS).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The only credential the skill needs is a Stripe restricted read key (STRIPE_READ_KEY), which is appropriate for read-only analytics. However, registry-level metadata incorrectly reported no required env vars while SKILL.md and package.json require STRIPE_READ_KEY. Confirm the platform enforces the gating that requires a restricted read-only key and that the skill will not be given broader credentials. Also verify that STRIPE_READ_KEY is indeed restricted to read scopes and that no other unrelated secrets are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request persistent system presence (always is false), does not declare writing to other skill configs, and SKILL.md claims no data storage. The code appears to return computed metrics without writing secrets to disk. Still verify runtime host enforces no unintended persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to check before installing:
- Fix the packaging/metadata mismatch: registry metadata should list STRIPE_READ_KEY and node if required; ask the author to correct it. The inconsistency is likely a packaging oversight but should be resolved.
- Ensure the STRIPE_READ_KEY you provide is a Stripe Restricted Key with only read:customers, read:subscriptions, read:invoices, read:payment_intents scope (no write/refund/charge scopes). Prefer the narrowest possible scope.
- Review the full skill/skill.js (the snippet was truncated) to confirm all outgoing network calls go only to https://api.stripe.com and there are no hidden endpoints or telemetry exfiltration.
- Verify the host execution model: since there is JS code bundled but no install spec, confirm how the platform will run skill/skill.js and whether it sandboxs network access and environment variables.
- Test in an isolated environment first (use a dummy Stripe restricted key or test-mode key) to confirm behavior and that no secrets are logged or persisted.
- If the registry metadata is corrected and the remaining code exclusively calls Stripe and returns aggregated metrics (no hidden endpoints, no unrelated env reads), this skill would appear coherent and lower risk.
If you want, I can list the exact lines to inspect in the full skill file (e.g., network targets, any use of process.env beyond STRIPE_READ_KEY, any fs or child_process usage) or help prepare safe tests to run with a test Stripe key.
